prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 16 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 4 panels across and 4 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a landscape 16:9 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Cash Van; image 2 is the reference sheet for phone. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: phone exactly as shown.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Dinu is the red mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one storyboard image containing sixteen equal landscape panels, four across and four down, in shot order, with narrow blank gutters and no drawn text, numbering or arrows. Dinu is a smooth, unmarked red artist's mannequin of medium-tall, lean proportions; the people inside the photograph remain photographic. The compact right-hand-drive van has a dark grey moulded dashboard, worn black vinyl seats, rubber floor mats and a solid steel partition behind the cab. A faded photograph is fixed to the central dashboard, with the same scuffed black smartphone secured immediately to its left throughout; a thin red thread circles Dinu's left wrist. Rain beads cover the glass at night. Cool green-blue instrument light and narrow sodium-orange light from the driver's side share a restrained 4300K mixed-light grade, with deep shadows and dense, soft exterior lights. Materials, prop positions and lighting remain consistent across the grid.

Geography: The entire sequence stays inside one connected cab as the van travels along wet Colombo streets. Dinu occupies the right-hand driving seat, with the wheel directly ahead, the photograph inward toward the cab centre and the phone just farther left within his left-hand reach. The passenger-side master looks diagonally across the cab: Dinu remains frame right, the wheel low centre, the dashboard and windscreen extend left, and the driver's rain-covered side window remains behind him on frame right. Tighter driving views remain on this passenger side of the axis; dashboard inserts look across the same arrangement without reversing the phone and photograph. Exterior streets remain indistinct until soft industrial structures first enter the windscreen view in panel fifteen; the final close view retains the same right-side window landmark on the new course.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Passenger-side three-quarter view at seated head height, looking diagonally toward the driving seat and forward glass; medium-wide seated framing, 35mm feel. Background: Wet windscreen and blurred city lights occupy frame left; the driver's wet side window is frame right, with a narrow dark partition edge at far right. Dinu sits frame right, his chest directed toward the wheel and diagonally screen left toward the road. His head follows that direction in three-quarter profile, and both hands hold the wheel low centre. The dashboard stretches across the left foreground, its small central fittings too indistinct to identify.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Passenger-side oblique view at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; medium close-up, 65mm feel. Background: The driver's rain-covered side window and crowded orange-blue light shapes remain frame right; the partition is a dark strip at far right. Dinu occupies centre-right, with his chest angled screen left toward the wheel and his head aligned toward the road in three-quarter profile. Both hands remain on the wheel at the lower edge of the panel. The upper wheel rim crosses the foreground without obscuring his head.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Forward passenger-side offset at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; tight head-and-shoulder close-up, 85mm feel, retaining a three-quarter angle. Background: A narrow strip of the driver's wet side window remains frame right, with small orange-blue light circles; the central dashboard is outside the crop to the left. Dinu's head and one shoulder fill the panel, his chest still aligned with the wheel toward screen left. His head remains turned toward the road, clearly offset from the lens rather than square to it. Both hands stay on the wheel below the crop.
PANEL 4 (row 1, column 4) — Dashboard-level oblique insert from the passenger side, looking across the fixed photograph; 75mm feel with enough depth to resolve the printed image. Background: Dark moulded dashboard surrounds the print; wet windscreen and soft city lights occupy the upper-left background, while the driver's side window stays outside the crop to the right. The faded photograph fills the centre as a visibly flat paper print fixed to the dashboard. Inside it, a real photographic Dinu and Aruni stand beside a simple village bus shelter, with any signage too soft to resolve. The secured phone's dark edge appears to the photograph's left.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 1) — Return to the passenger-side three-quarter master at seated head height; medium shot, 35mm feel. Background: Wet windscreen and soft street lights remain left; the driver's rain-covered side window remains right, with the partition edge at far right. Dinu sits frame right with his chest and head directed diagonally screen left toward the road, both hands holding the wheel. The faded photograph is identifiable as a fixed paper object low left, though its two figures are too small to resolve at this scale. The secured phone sits immediately to its left with a dark, unreadable display.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 2) — Dashboard-level oblique insert from the established passenger side, framed farther left around the phone; 75mm feel. Background: The dashboard forms the immediate background, with wet windscreen blur upper left; the photograph's cropped edge is right of the phone, and the driver's side window remains outside frame right. The secured phone fills the centre with a large triangular playback control on its otherwise simple, unlettered screen. Dinu's left hand begins on the wheel at the right edge, with the red thread visible around that wrist. His torso and right hand are outside the crop.
PANEL 7 (row 2, column 3) — Same passenger-side forward offset as panel three, at seated head height approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; close-up, 85mm feel. Background: The driver's wet side window remains a narrow strip on frame right, carrying compressed orange-blue light shapes; the dashboard stays outside frame left. Dinu's head and shoulder fill the centre, his chest directed toward the wheel and diagonally screen left. His head stays aligned toward the road in three-quarter view, away from the lens. Both hands remain on the wheel below the panel edge.
PANEL 8 (row 2, column 4) — Established passenger-side oblique position at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; medium close-up, 65mm feel. Background: The rain-covered driver's side window remains frame right behind Dinu, with the partition a dark sliver at far right. Dinu sits centre-right with his chest facing the wheel toward screen left and his head turned along the same roadward direction. Both hands hold the wheel at the bottom edge, with the upper rim visible between his forearms. His head remains in three-quarter profile, separate from the soft wet lights behind.
PANEL 9 (row 3, column 1) — Established forward passenger-side offset at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; tight close-up, 85mm feel. Dinu's head fills the centre above a small portion of shoulder, with his chest still directed diagonally screen left toward the wheel. His head remains roadward in three-quarter view rather than turning toward the camera. Both hands stay on the wheel below frame.
PANEL 10 (row 3, column 2) — Dashboard-level oblique insert from the same passenger-side position as the earlier phone insert; 75mm feel. Background: Dark moulded dashboard surrounds the handset; the photograph's edge remains to its right, wet windscreen blur is upper left, and the driver's side window is outside frame right. The same secured phone fills the centre with an incoming-call layout on a softly lit dark screen. A blank caller band sits above large green and red circular controls, without lettering or a portrait. No hand enters the panel.
PANEL 11 (row 3, column 3) — Return to the passenger-side three-quarter master at seated head height; medium shot, 35mm feel. Background: Wet windscreen and city lights remain frame left; the driver's wet side window remains frame right, with the steel partition at far right. Dinu occupies frame right, his chest facing the wheel and diagonally screen left toward the road. Both hands begin on the wheel, while his head remains roadward in three-quarter profile. The secured phone displays its unlettered incoming-call layout low left, with the small faded photograph immediately to its right.
PANEL 12 (row 3, column 4) — Established forward passenger-side offset at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; close-up, 85mm feel. Background: The driver's wet side window stays frame right, its rain-lit points compressed into small soft shapes; the dashboard is outside frame left. Dinu's head and shoulder fill the panel, with his chest kept toward the wheel at screen left. His head stays roadward in three-quarter view, not square to the lens. PANEL 13 (row 4, column 1) — Established passenger-side oblique position at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; medium close-up, 65mm feel. Dinu sits centre-right with his chest directed diagonally screen left toward the wheel. His head remains turned toward the road in three-quarter profile, and both hands hold the wheel along the lower edge. The central dashboard props lie outside this tighter crop to the left.
PANEL 14 (row 4, column 2) — Passenger-side oblique position at seated head height; medium shot widened to include both hands and the upper wheel, 50mm feel. Background: The driver's rain-streaked side window stays frame right, with ordinary city-light blur behind it; the dashboard extends off frame left. Dinu sits centre-right, his chest facing the wheel toward screen left and his head still directed toward the road at this opening instant. Both hands hold the wheel low centre, with the red thread clearly visible around his left wrist. His head, wrist and wheel are all contained in the same composition.
PANEL 15 (row 4, column 3) — Established passenger-side three-quarter master at seated head height; medium-wide seated framing including the road ahead, 35mm feel. Background: The wet road occupies the windscreen on frame left, with the first soft industrial rooflines beyond it; the driver's wet side window remains frame right and the partition stays far right. Dinu sits frame right with his chest and head directed diagonally screen left toward the road. Both hands hold the wheel in its original-course position at this opening instant, with the red thread around the left wrist. The phone and small faded photograph remain fixed on the central dashboard low left, while distant industrial structures are soft through the rain-covered windscreen.
PANEL 16 (row 4, column 4) — Established forward passenger-side offset at seated head height, approximately 1.15 metres above the cab floor; tight close-up, 85mm feel. Background: The driver's wet side-window strip remains frame right, now containing sparse, soft industrial light points; the central dashboard stays outside frame left. Dinu's head and shoulder fill the centre, his chest directed toward the wheel and diagonally screen left. His head remains roadward in three-quarter view, offset from the lens. Both hands hold the wheel below the crop on the new course.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
